sources.title: Gretzinger and colleagues, Ancient DNA connects large-scale migration with the spread of Slavs
sources.note: 2025 Nature study of 555 ancient individuals, population movement, regional integration, pedigrees, and identity limits.

sources.title: Florin Curta, From Kossinna to Bromley: ethnogenesis and early Slavic archaeology
sources.note: Peer-reviewed historiographic critique of national origin stories, archaeological labels, migration models, and sixth-century sources.

sources.title: Zbigniew Kobylinski, The Slavs
sources.note: Cambridge history chapter on sixth-century texts, linguistic reconstruction, archaeology, settlement, politics, and regional development.

sources.title: Chemical and isotopic analyses confirm dietary change during Slavic expansion
sources.note: Peer-reviewed pottery lipid, isotope, archaeobotanical, and chronological evidence from Moravia and Lower Austria.

sources.title: Kuna and Profantova, Prague-Type Culture Houses
sources.note: Original archaeological study of more than three hundred Roztoky houses, stone ovens, postholes, use, and abandonment.

sources.title: Charcoal analyses of Early Medieval house fills at Roztoky
sources.note: Peer-reviewed environmental and taphonomic analysis of house fills, charcoal, settlement duration, and woodland use.

sources.title: Henning Andersen, The Slavic Expansion: Streams, Springs, and Wells
sources.note: Interdisciplinary study of settlement by watercourses, natural springs, hand-dug wells, and historical water vocabulary.

sources.title: From Water Source to Sedimentary Archive at Pohansko
sources.note: Masaryk University research record for a seventh- to eighth-century well, flooding, husbandry, plants, and waste management.

sources.title: Characteristics of the Oldest Slavic Pottery at Nova Tabla
sources.note: Original study of sixth- to early ninth-century settlement horizons, handmade pottery, fabrics, firing, and technological change.

sources.title: Early Slavs production and subsistence in the Upper Tisza basin
sources.note: Peer-reviewed regional case study of agriculture, domestic crafts, tools, iron utensils, and possible specialization.

sources.title: The Slavic expansion: smiths, smithies, and smelters
sources.note: 2026 interdisciplinary article connecting archaeological ironworking evidence with historically reconstructed craft vocabulary.

sources.title: Ancient genomes and demographic change in Moravia
sources.note: Open primary genomic study with Early Hillfort chronology, burial contexts, and the cremation-related sampling gap.

sources.title: Machacek and colleagues, Runes from Lany
sources.note: Primary Journal of Archaeological Science study of a radiocarbon-dated cattle rib and incomplete Elder Futhark exercise.

sources.title: Prehistory to History: knowledge transmission and literacy in Central Europe
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis distinguishing rare early script contact from ninth-century institutional literary culture.

sources.title: Oxford Research Archive, Old Church Slavonic
sources.note: University encyclopedia entry identifying Old Church Slavonic as the earliest Slavic literary language from the ninth century.

sources.title: University of Texas, Introduction to Old Church Slavonic
sources.note: University linguistics reference separating reconstructed Proto-Slavic from the oldest documented Slavic language and later manuscripts.

sources.title: Environmental stress in the Early Mediaeval Slavic population at Borovce
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of enamel hypoplasia in an eighth- to twelfth-century skeletal series, with diagnostic limits.

sources.title: Dental health at the Late Antique to Early Medieval transition in Croatia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed comparison of caries, tooth loss, abscesses, calculus, resorption, and wear in composite skeletal samples.

sources.title: Health at the sixth- to eighth-century child cemetery at Sipar
sources.note: Institutional record for preliminary macroscopic and genomic study of eighteen infants from a mixed regional context.

sources.title: Navigating the Flames: Early Medieval cremation practices
sources.note: 2026 Archaeometry comparison of pyre conditions, cremated remains, ritual variability, and chronological uncertainty.

sources.title: Bilogrivic, Urns, Slavs, and Croats
sources.note: Original study separating cremation evidence, uncertain dating, migration, and later ethnic or national labels.

sources.title: Curta, Slavs in Fredegar: medieval gens or narrative strategy?
sources.note: University repository article analyzing Samo, Wends, Slavs, political terminology, and the chronicler narrative strategy.

sources.title: Curta, Kings and democracy: power in early Slavic society
sources.note: Cambridge chapter reassessing Procopius, collective decision making, leaders, warfare, and simplistic democracy stereotypes.

sources.title: Denis Sinor, The Avars
sources.note: Cambridge history chapter on Avar chronology, rule, source limitations, and interaction across Central Europe.

sources.title: How the East Became the East in Carolingian Central Europe
sources.note: Recent peer-reviewed account of eighth-century Slavic settlement, the Avar frontier, Carolingian campaigns, and political reorganization.

sources.title: Gustin, The Early Middle Ages from the Alpine Slopes to Pannonia
sources.note: Original archaeological synthesis of sixth- and seventh-century settlements, radiocarbon dates, and regional pottery sequences.
